instructions: Pull the skin off the chicken thighs. Put them in a large pot with the onion cut in half, the bay leaves, cinnamon stick, cardamom pods, cloves, 1 tsp of the salt and 6 cups of water.

Bring to a boil, skim off the foam, then turn the heat to low and simmer, partly covered, for 35 minutes. You're cooking the chicken to 175°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check it there. No thermometer? Cut into the thickest thigh: it's done when the juices run clear.

Meanwhile, pick any stems out of the molokhia leaves. Soak the leaves in warm water with 1 tbsp of lemon juice for 20 minutes. Rinse, then squeeze handfuls until the water runs clear. Pat them dry with a clean towel and fluff them apart.

Finely chop the cilantro leaves. Mince the garlic and mix it with the cilantro in a bowl. Crush the coriander seeds with the flat of a knife or in a mortar. Thinly slice the chili and set it aside for the table.

Transfer the chicken to a plate and strain the broth into a bowl. That should be about 5 cups. Add water if it's short. When the chicken is cool enough to handle, shred the meat and throw away the bones.

Rinse the rice in cold water 3 or 4 times, until the water runs clear. Break the vermicelli into short pieces. Heat 2 tbsp of the oil in a medium pot over medium-high heat, add the vermicelli, and stir for 2 minutes, until golden. Add the rice, stir for 1 minute, then add 2 1/4 cups of water and 1 tsp of the salt. Bring to a boil, turn the heat to low, cover, and cook for 15 minutes. Leave it covered off the heat until you serve.
Heat 2 tbsp of the oil in a wide pot over medium heat. Add the crushed coriander seeds and stir for 30 seconds. Add the leaves in handfuls and stir for 3 minutes. Transfer them to a bowl.
Add the last 2 tbsp oil to the same pot. Add two thirds of the garlic and cilantro mix and cook for 2 minutes, until fragrant. Add the leaves back and stir until they're coated.
Add 4 cups of the hot broth, the shredded chicken, the juice of the 2 lemons (minus the 1 tbsp used for soaking) and the last 1 tsp salt. Simmer gently for 20 minutes. Don't let it boil hard.
Stir in the rest of the garlic and cilantro mix for the last 5 minutes.
Ladle the mloukhieh over the vermicelli rice. Serve with the sliced chili on the side for anyone who wants heat.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt or a squeeze of lemon.
method_notes: None of the versions read has 20 or more ratings (Alphafoodie's Mom's Authentic Lebanese Molokhia 5.0 from 11 votes, Taste Great Foodie 5.0 from 4), so the lead is the best-read real version and fallback is marked. The sources agree on whole jute leaves sauteed in oil, a heavy garlic and cilantro base, a chicken broth and lemon, simmered gently and served over vermicelli rice. They differ on a whole chicken versus parts, soaking time, and how much garlic. Pomona uses bone-in thighs instead of a whole chicken to save time, keeps the chili out of the pot and puts it on the side, and uses dried leaves (frozen whole leaves work too, skip the soak).
